m: śyena m. a hawk, falcon, eagle, any bird of prey (esp. the eagle that brings down Soma to man), RV. &c. &c.
firewood laid in the shape of an eagle, Śulbas.
a kind of array (in battle), MBh.; Kām.
a partic. part of the sacrificial victim, Kauś.
N. of a Ṛṣi (having the patr. Āgneya and author of RV. x, 188), Anukr.
(with or without indraśya) N. of a Sāman, ĀrṣBr.; Lāṭy.
coming from an eagle (as ‘eagle's flesh’), Kṛṣṇaj. (prob. w.r. for śyaina).
a: śyenaḥ [śyai-inan] 1 The white colour. 2 Whiteness. 3 A hawk, falcon. 4 Violence. 5 Ved. A horse. Comp. — avapātaḥ the swoop of a hawk; Māl. 8. 8. — karaṇaṃ, — karaṇikā 1 burning on a separate funeral pile. 2 a hawk-like, i. e. rash and desperate, act. — cit, -jīvin m. a falconer.
